headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from shared filesystem/MCP and broad egress; compliance exposure is also material.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code reads workspace files and uses MCP/browsers; aci can emit CRM/email/calendar outputs and also uses MCP. Because Roo Code shares state via filesystem and can ingest file content, attacker-controlled content from aci outputs can be treated as instructions. The interaction is documented enough to assess, and the shared channel makes hijack plausible by default.
conditions: IF aci writes untrusted text into a workspace file that Roo Code later reads
IF Roo Code is configured to parse file contents or MCP payloads as instructions
mitigations: Keep aci outputs out of shared workspace files
Use a separate read-only handoff directory
Require explicit human review before Roo Code acts on aci-generated text
Disable automatic instruction-following on imported files
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, support, and research data, while Roo Code has broad filesystem read/write plus browser screenshots and broad network egress. Shared workspace state and model/API calls create a realistic path for sensitive data to leave the pair, especially if Roo Code reads aci-produced artifacts or logs. The blast radius includes customer and email data.
conditions: IF aci stores CRM or email content in files accessible to Roo Code
IF Roo Code forwards workspace contents or screenshots to its model API or MCP servers
mitigations: Separate sensitive aci data from Roo Code workspaces
Redact CRM/email fields before file handoff
Restrict Roo Code network access during shared tasks
Review browser screenshots before upload
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write to shared mutable resources: aci via APIs like Google Sheets/CRM/email and Roo Code via filesystem, git, shell, and MCP. Roo Code explicitly shares state with other instances via filesystem, so concurrent edits can collide with aci-driven updates. Without locking, overlapping writes can corrupt files or remote records.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same workspace files or git branch
IF aci and Roo Code update the same CRM or spreadsheet records without coordination
mitigations: Assign one writer per resource
Pause one agent during the other's write phase
Use branch-per-agent workflows
Add manual lock files for shared directories
requires-engineering: implement transactional coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and Roo Code can execute shell, git, browser, and MCP actions. If Roo Code treats aci output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious aci result can cascade into irreversible commits, emails, or external API calls. The pair therefore has a direct action-taking chain with no built-in verification shown.
conditions: IF Roo Code consumes aci output without a verification step
IF aci output is used to trigger shell, git, email, or MCP actions
mitigations: Require a second-pass verification prompt
Block auto-execution of aci-derived commands
Use dry-run mode for git and shell actions
Log and diff all aci-to-Roo handoffs
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoff payloads

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles email, CRM, customer support, and calendar data, while Roo Code handles source code and browser screenshots with broad egress. The pair can mix regulated customer data with code and screenshots, creating retention and residency ambiguity even though no specific jurisdiction or certification mismatch is documented. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF customer support or email data is copied into Roo Code screenshots or workspace files
IF the deployment stores aci data and Roo Code artifacts under different retention policies
mitigations: Classify shared artifacts before transfer
Exclude regulated fields from screenshots
Set a short retention window for shared workspaces
Document deletion/export handling for both tools
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
